newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 17.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
LEFT PARTIES HARP ON WITHDRAWAL OF LETTER

The Left constituents of the ruling coalition, in an attempt to buy more time, asked Congress to send a fresh letter to the president withdrawing the earlier one that pulled down the government. The Left, after deliberating on the current developments, had felt the need for Congress to take some steps before the United Front changed its leader. It also asked Congress president Sitaram Kesri to follow it up with another letter pledging support to the United Front if it was to form a new government.
The Hindustan Times
MECCA FIRE TOLL 343

At least 343 people were killed in a huge fire that ripped through pilgrims' tents near Mecca, Saudi authorities announced. The death toll was expected to rise as many of the injured were in serious condition. The exact nationalities of the victims was still being established and would be announced later. Indian officials said 250 people were killed of whom 150 were Indians. The fire was believed to have broken out in Pakistani camps following a gas cylinder burst. The exact cause of the fire, however, was being ascertained.
The Economic Times
INDIA AMONG FASTEST-GROWING TRADERS

India is among the fastest growing traders for 1990-96 with an average annual growth rate of 11 percent for this period, a study prepared by the World Trade Organisation secretariat said. The fastest trader for the period, according to the study, was Malaysia with 18 percent average annual growth. The study also ranked India as the 29th largest importer in 1996, with imports at $37.5 billion. However, India did not figure in the list of top 30 exporters put up by the secretariat. Indian exports for this period were around $32 billion.
COLLISION AVOIDANCE SYSTEM MUST FOR ALL AIRCRAFT

India will make it mandatory for all aircraft in the country, and those coming in, to carry the Airborne Collision Avoidance System (ACAS) from January 1, 1999. This was in view of the number of near-air misses and congestion of airspace in the country. Presently, only the United States makes it mandatory for aircraft to carry the system. Aircraft with more then 30 seats which do not carry ACAS would not be allowed into Indian airspace from January 1, 1999.
UB GROUP MOVES GLOBAL OPERATIONS OUT OF DUBAI

Vijay Mallya's UB Group has shifted its international operations from Dubai to South Africa and the United States. Key Dubai-based group executives were either relocated to India, South Africa, USA or quit. With the sale of Berger International in August 1996, the group has had no significant operations in Dubai, sources said. Its operating subsidiaries in West Asia, Malta, and Far-East were consolidated under Berger International. Paints was the group's main activity in the Gulf region, and with Berger being sold, its Dubai exposure stood reduced.
ADB EXPECTS INDIAN INDUSTRY TO GROW BY 11.7 PCT

The Asian Development Bank (ADB) expected Indian industry to grow by 11.7 percent in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) and 1998/99. The services sector, which accounted for more than 40 percent of gross domestic product, was expected to grow by around 6.5 percent during this period. But the bank said inadequate infrastructure was an area of concern. It said there were major constraints in the power, transport and telecommunications sectors.
Financial Express
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS MAY BE ALLOWED ACCESS TO BANK FUNDS

The central bank (RBI) planned to pull down the barrier between banks and financial institutions (FIs) by allowing FIs to access bank funds. It also suggested that FIs should consider functioning like banks. RBI was also in the process of drawing up plans to enable FIs to provide greater access to markets for cheaper resource mobilisation. The RBI governor said the central bank had already initiated a dialogue with the FIs in this regard. The objective was to enable the institutions to bring down the cost of funds and consequently their lending rates.
BAIL-OUT PLAN FOR ITC CLASSIC

The ITC board, deliberating on the revival plan for ITC Classic, agreed to acquire all investments of the troubled financial services unit in unrelated areas like real estate and a host of unlisted companies which did not fit into the main business of Classic. Among the assets being contemplated for acquisition was the Bombay real estate held by Classic Infrastructure Development.
Business Standard
GOVERNMENT BANKING ON WHEAT PRICE CRASH

Despite the call for a boycott of the grain markets, government agencies may be able to mop up wheat in Punjab because growers would have to sell their produce to official agencies to raise cash. The bulk of procurement was expected from interior areas where neither traders nor farm unions were likely to be very active. Both agriculture experts and farmers felt prices would crash to the minimum support price level by the third week of this month, leaving farmers' no option but to sell their produce to the Food Corporation of India and state grain procuring agencies.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS FEAR EXODUS OF TOP CORPORATES

Financial institutions (FIs) fear losing top corporate clients to banks due to the incentives and operational freedom granted to the latter in the central bank's slack season credit policy. With banks now in a position to charge 2-3 percent less from corporate clients, difference between the lending rates charged by banks and FIs was expected to double to 2-4 percent. This was because the cost of funds for banks was expected to come down by nearly two percent from 11-12 percent at present, while FIs were raising money from the bond market at 16.5-17 percent.
NON BANK ENTITIES MAY BE ALLOWED TO ENTER INTO REPOS

The Governor of the Reserve bank hinted at deepening the money market further by allowing even non-bank entities to enter into repos. He said the decision on reducing interest rates on non-resident (external) rupee deposits was part of the RBI's policy of rationalising interest rates structures for domestic and non resident Indian deposits. He said the decision to allow authorised dealers to borrow and invest up to $10 million in foreign markets was a relaxation in capital transactions.
UNIT TRUST MAY GAIN FROM TAX SOP ON DIVIDEND

With the budget abolishing double taxation of dividends, several schemes of the Unit Trust of India (UTI) would regain their place as favoured instruments of investment. The budget abolished double taxation of dividends and replaced it with a tax on distributed profits. The move would provide a major avenue for companies to earn tax-free income to shore up their bottom lines and was likely to lead to a flight of savings away from other instruments like bank deposits and government bonds.
The Observer
INDUSTRY MINISTRY FOR SAY IN LIQUOR LICENCES

In a bid to regain its authority over issuing licences for potable liquor, the Industry Ministry sought the Law Ministry's help in exploring legal avenues to restore status quo ante. A Supreme Court judgement in January had ruled that the federal government did not have powers to permit or prohibit setting up of industries for manufacturing rectified spirit meant for potable purpose. The ruling also held liquor production to be a state subject. Following this, the industry ministry refused to grant licence or permission for setting up liquor manufacturing units.
